//: fluidbox qwen-runner SYSTEM-scope settings — the governance analogue of the codex image's config.toml. Baked root-owned READ-ONLY and pointed at by QWEN_CODE_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH; system scope outranks workspace/user scopes for scalars and the permissions arrays merge as a UNION (lower scopes can only ADD rules, and ask beats allow), so a repo-committed .qwen/settings.json cannot relax any of this. Verified against the pinned @qwen-code/qwen-code@0.21.1 — see docs/research/2026-07-30-qwen-code-sdk-protocol.md.

tools.//approvalMode: The upstream DEFAULT is 'auto' — an LLM classifier that auto-approves 'safe' calls, bypassing the gate AND burning facade calls. 'default' routes every confirmation to the SDK channel (canUseTool).
tools.//sandbox: The fluidbox container IS the sandbox; qwen's own nesting (docker/podman) is impossible under cap_drop=ALL anyway.
tools.//disabled: Unregisters the tool entirely (stronger than a deny rule: it never appears in the model's schema). PROVEN TRAP: disabling tool_search surfaces the deferred-tool registry (computer_use__*, cron_*, send_message, …) directly into the schema — so every deferred/agentic tool is disabled EXPLICITLY alongside it. agent/subagents are killed because inner tool calls degrade to deny without individual gating; web_fetch is ON upstream by default and must die (egress-free sandbox). With this list the live census is EXACTLY the nine core tools: edit, glob, grep_search, list_directory, notebook_edit, read_file, run_shell_command, todo_write, write_file.

permissions.//ask: THE interception closure (rule priority deny > ask > allow > mode default): read-only tools default to 'allow' and would otherwise execute without ever reaching canUseTool. An ask rule forces the confirmation, which the SDK channel routes to canUseTool → the fluidbox /permission gate. Both the alias meta-categories AND the raw tool names are listed (union-merged) so neither an alias-semantics change nor a raw-name change can silently open a gap alone; 'mcp__' prefix-matches every MCP tool. PROVEN LIVE: read_file crosses canUseTool under this config, and an SDK allow maps to proceed_once — never a persistent grant.
